title: Classic Tuna Tartare with Lime, Capers, Avocado and Radish
summary: Finely diced raw tuna dressed with lime, olive oil, capers, chilli and coriander, moulded into rounds and served with fanned avocado, radish and chives.

ingredients.item: small red onion, very finely diced
green chilli, deseeded and finely chopped
fine sea salt or table salt

steps.title: Mellow the onion
steps.text: Cover the diced onion with cold water for 5 min, then drain and pat it dry. The soak takes off its sharp edge so it does not overpower the tuna.

steps.title: Dice the tuna
steps.text: Cut the fish into 5 mm slices, then strips, then small, even cubes, and keep them in the bowl over ice. Even pieces give a neat look and a pleasant texture.

steps.title: Whisk the dressing
steps.text: Combine the lime juice, oil, garlic, chilli, capers, salt and pepper in the small bowl.

steps.title: Mix at the last minute
steps.text: No more than 10 min before eating, fold the dressing, onion and coriander through the tuna and leave it in the fridge for 5 min. Much longer and the lime begins to cure the fish, turning it opaque.

steps.title: Mould and serve
steps.text: Press a quarter of the tartare into the ring on each cold plate and lift it off. Slice the avocado, brush it with lime to stop browning, fan it beside the tartare and top with radish slices and chives.

tips: A common mistake is using a food processor, which turns the tuna into a paste; dice it by hand.
Sashimi-grade salmon works in exactly the same way.
Wipe the ring between portions for clean edges.
safety: RAW NOTE: the fish is eaten raw. Buy sushi- or sashimi-grade fish from a fishmonger you trust that has been frozen first (-20 °C for 7 days or -35 °C for 15 hours), keep it in the fridge until the last minute and eat it the same day. Pregnant people, young children, older adults and anyone with weakened immunity should skip it.
storage: Fish tartare must be eaten straight away; discard any leftovers. Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
